staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced the crash from this preserved checkout. The saved symbolized trace names `xmlXIncludeLoadFallback` at `xinclude.c:1987`, `xmlXIncludeLoadNode` at `xinclude.c:2150`, `xmlXIncludeDoProcess` at `xinclude.c:2449`, `xmlStaticCopyNode` at `tree.c:4360`, `xmlStaticCopyNodeList` at `tree.c:4430`, `xmlFreeDoc` at `tree.c:1250`, and the final bad-free sink at `xmlFreeNodeList` line 3750.

classification.classification_note: The saved witness reaches recursive XInclude fallback processing with attacker-controlled old-namespace (`http://www.w3.org/2001/XInclude`) markup and an `href` beginning `#xpointer`. That old namespace flips `ctxt->legacy` on, letting `xmlXIncludeAddNode` treat the URI fragment as the include fragment instead of rejecting it. Vulnerable XInclude code then accepts XPointer location objects (`XPATH_RANGE` / `XPATH_LOCATIONSET`), materializes them into replacement nodes, and splices that list into the fallback subtree before outer fallback copying reaches the recorded bad-free in `xmlFreeNodeList`.

bug_description.original: Invalid free and uninitialized-value in XInclude processing: while processing XInclude nodes (xmlXIncludeDoProcess in xinclude.c), libxml2's node-copy/free path (xmlStaticCopyNode/xmlFreeNode/xmlFreeNodeList/xmlFreeDoc in tree.c) attempts to free a pointer that was not returned by malloc (free on an interior address of an allocated block), causing heap corruption and crashes. MSAN also reports a use-of-uninitialized-value in the same XInclude/doc node creation path (xmlDictLookup/xmlNewDocNode), leading to undefined behavior and further memory corruption risk.
bug_description.normalized: The staged `poc` is a libxml2 `fuzz/xml` container whose first four bytes decode to the little-endian option word `0x78232467`. The extracted main-entity payload is malformed but still contains fallback content, old-namespace XInclude markup (`http://www.w3.org/2001/XInclude`), and at least one `xi:include` whose `href` begins with `#xpointer`. On the witnessed path, outer fallback handling recursively reprocesses that fallback subtree; the nested XInclude pass sets `ctxt->legacy = 1` for the old namespace, records the `href` fragment as the include fragment, evaluates it with `xmlXPtrEval`, and accepts a location-style XPointer result (`XPATH_RANGE` or `XPATH_LOCATIONSET`) for copying. XInclude then materializes that location result into a replacement node list, splices that list into the fallback subtree in place, and outer fallback handling copies the now-mutated `fallback->children` with `xmlDocCopyNodeList`. The saved AddressSanitizer trace shows the failure unwinding through `xmlStaticCopyNode` into `xmlFreeNode` / `xmlFreeDoc`, ending at `xmlFreeNodeList` line 3750 where a node `name` pointer located 87 bytes inside an `xmlDictAddString` allocation is freed as though it were standalone heap memory.

source.description: First project-side state creation on the witnessed crashing path. During recursive fallback reprocessing, XInclude sees attacker-controlled old-namespace markup (`http://www.w3.org/2001/XInclude`) and enables legacy mode, which is the condition that later makes the `href` URI fragment admissible as the include fragment.
source.value_from: Decoding the staged `poc` as a `fuzz/xml` container shows repeated `http://www.w3.org/2001/XInclude` strings together with `#xpointer`-prefixed include targets inside fallback content. This assignment is the first project statement on the crashing path that turns that markup into vulnerability-relevant parser state.

root_cause.description: Root cause supported by the staged patch. Vulnerable XInclude processing accepts XPointer location objects and routes them into the node-copy path even though that path can produce text-node layouts that later violate the copy/free invariants in `tree.c`.
root_cause.note: The staged fix wraps the XPointer location support with `LIBXML_XPTR_LOCS_ENABLED` and disables it by default, removing these `XPATH_RANGE` / `XPATH_LOCATIONSET` branches from the default XInclude path. Stage 02 did not execute the fixed build, so this is source-grounded rather than dynamically revalidated.

sink.description: Crash sink. While unwinding a failed subtree copy, `xmlFreeNodeList` frees a node `name` pointer that actually points inside a dictionary string pool allocation, matching AddressSanitizer's saved bad-free report.

parser_admitted.description: Project-code parser gate for the staged witness's main XML entity. The malformed container payload still has to present a document body beginning with `<` so libxml2 enters element parsing and builds the XInclude nodes later consumed by `xmlXIncludeAddNode`.

tainted_value_origin.description: This assignment preserves the attacker-controlled XPointer fragment inside the XInclude reference record so the later load phase can evaluate it and enter the location-object copy path.

coarse_trace.summary: After an outer include load fails, fallback handling recursively reprocesses the fallback subtree so nested XInclude nodes inside that fallback are scanned and processed.
In that nested pass, attacker-controlled old-namespace XInclude markup sets `ctxt->legacy = 1`, allowing `xmlXIncludeAddNode` to accept the `href` URI fragment and store it as the include fragment.
The nested include load evaluates that fragment as an XPointer, vulnerable code accepts location-style results, and XInclude materializes them into replacement nodes.

Nested inclusion splices those replacement nodes into the fallback subtree in place, then outer fallback handling copies the mutated subtree and rollback through the copy/free path reaches the recorded bad-free.

fine_trace.note: Outer fallback handling explicitly re-enters XInclude processing on the fallback subtree. The remaining steps occur during this nested `xmlXIncludeDoProcess(newctxt, ..., fallback, 1)` pass before control returns to the outer fallback copy at line 1987.

Source. In the nested fallback pass, the attacker-controlled include node uses `XINCLUDE_OLD_NS` (`http://www.w3.org/2001/XInclude`), so XInclude enables legacy mode for this context. That state is what later allows a URI fragment in `href` to be reused as the include fragment.

During that same nested pass, XInclude reads the attacker-controlled include target from the parsed `xi:include` element. On the witnessed path, this `href` begins with the crafted local `#xpointer...` fragment.

depends_on.via: xmlXIncludeTestNode accepted the old-namespace include node

fine_trace.note: Because legacy mode is already enabled, `xmlXIncludeAddNode` does not reject the `href` fragment. Instead it reuses `uri->fragment` as the include fragment, turning the attacker-controlled `#xpointer...` suffix into the value that will drive XPointer evaluation.
The nested include setup stores that attacker-controlled fragment in the `xmlXIncludeRef` record retained by the XInclude context, preserving it for the later load phase.
The load phase evaluates the stored attacker-controlled fragment as an XPointer expression and materializes the result in `xptr`.
Root cause. Vulnerable XInclude processing explicitly admits location-style XPointer results and continues toward the copy routines instead of rejecting them like the scalar cases above.

The admitted XPointer location result is materialized into an ordinary replacement node list and stored as the nested include's replacement subtree. This is the XPointer-locations path disabled by the staged fix.

The nested third phase consumes that replacement list and splices its nodes into the fallback subtree in place. After this insertion, the outer `fallback->children` list being copied later at line 1987 contains XPointer-derived nodes rather than just the original nested include element.

depends_on.via: recursive fallback pass reaches third-phase inclusion

fine_trace.note: Outer fallback handling duplicates the now-mutated fallback child list into a fresh replacement subtree. The crash stack reaches this exact statement immediately before descending into `xmlStaticCopyNodeList` / `xmlStaticCopyNode`.

While copying child nodes, `xmlStaticCopyNode` may coalesce a just-copied text node into the previous sibling and return the existing node instead of the fresh `ret`. This is the load-bearing text-coalescing behavior called out by the nearby source comment.

On the saved crashing path, subtree copying unwinds through this rollback edge in `xmlStaticCopyNode`. The saved stack places this frame directly above `xmlFreeNode`, `xmlFreeNodeList`, and `xmlFreeDoc` in the bad-free chain.

Sink. Rollback reaches `xmlFreeNodeList`, where `DICT_FREE` decides to free `cur->name`; ASan reports that pointer is 87 bytes inside an `xmlDictAddString` allocation from `xmlDictLookup`, so this free targets an interior dictionary string rather than malloc-owned storage.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch is source-consistent with this trace because it gates the `XPATH_RANGE` / `XPATH_LOCATIONSET` branches behind `LIBXML_XPTR_LOCS_ENABLED` and disables that feature by default, removing the location-object copy path that feeds the crash. Stage 02 did not execute the fixed build, so no dynamic fixed-side claim is made here.
sanitizer_ground_truth.source: staged sanitizer_trace.txt, default_crash_trace.txt, reproduction_report.json, exact staged source, patch.diff, the preserved `poc`, and the local repository history around the `xmlStaticCopyNode` regression

poc.trigger: Stage 01 reproduced `AddressSanitizer: attempting free on address which was not malloc()-ed` and saved the symbolized stack ending at `xmlFreeNodeList` line 3750 during XInclude fallback processing.

format.name: libxml2 `fuzz/xml` container
format.contract: The verified trigger is the exact staged witness at `gt_results/secbench_oss_libxml2.ossfuzz-42510687/poc`. Its load-bearing structure is: a four-byte little-endian option word `0x78232467`; then fuzz-container string records whose main XML entity contains fallback content, old-namespace XInclude markup (`http://www.w3.org/2001/XInclude`), and at least one `xi:include` with an `href` beginning `#xpointer`. This Stage 02 trace is grounded only for that exact preserved witness shape and does not generalize beyond it.
